subject: Re: Post-call recap — Acme Health private deployment / VPC options
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Acme Health private deployment / VPC options

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and agreed as next steps so we’re all aligned.

Pain points / drivers you shared:
- Primary: PHI + regulated workloads require US-only data residency and strict audit controls.
- Networking: your infra team prefers no outbound internet from inference cluster (air-gapped or tightly restricted egress).
- Security: customer-managed KMS/HSM for keys, full audit logs, and SOC2 artifacts for vendor assessment.
- Operational: predictable latency for interactive triage workflows (p99 < 250ms target) and throughput for nightly batch scoring.

Goals we discussed:
- Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) to meet residency / network controls.
- Pilot with subset of models + canary traffic in ~8–12 weeks (target: end of Q2).
- Technical deep-dive with Acme infra and security next week to confirm connectivity and certs.

Initial answers and assumptions from our side:
- We support Private (VPC) deployment and an on-prem air-gapped package.
- For VPC-only with no public egress, we can use VPC endpoints (S3, ECR) and a customer-provided KMS/HSM integration.
- If truly air-gapped (no outbound), we provide an offline install bundle and an on-site deployment path; will require a brief services engagement.

Requested next steps (action items):
1) Schedule 60m technical deep-dive: include Michael (infra) + your security owner. Proposed slots Tue/Wed next week — please confirm.
2) I’ll share a short deploy checklist and network requirements (ports, endpoints, CIDR guidance) — attached.
3) We’ll send SOC2 + compliance artifacts and a draft SOW/quote for pilot.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-overview.pdf (high-level), redwood-deploy-checklist.xlsx (initial ask list).

If I missed anything important from today’s call, please flag and I’ll update.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Acme Health private deployment / VPC options

Samantha — great questions. Looping in Dev (solutions) to confirm the specifics below and to run the technical deep-dive next week. I’ll also bring our security lead if helpful.

High-level answers (we’ll expand in the deep-dive and share a short tech note):
- Air-gapped installs: supported. We provide an offline installation bundle for fully air-gapped environments; this typically entails a short professional services engagement to transfer models and installers.
- VPC-only w/ restricted egress: supported via VPC endpoints (S3, ECR). Minimal required outbound is zero if you use endpoints. If you want managed updates/metrics over the internet we can optionally enable restricted egress to specific Redwood IP ranges.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations (PKCS#11). For Luna we’ve done integrations in previous deployments.
- Audit logs: logs can be stored in your account (S3) or forwarded to your SIEM via private endpoints; retention policy is customer-configurable.

Action items we’ll take before the deep-dive:
- Dev will send a short networking/ports note and a minimal CIDR list.
- I’ll upload SOC2 + compliance summary to the Drive link and share the HubSpot deal record.

Proposed tech deep-dive: Tue 2026-03-17 at 14:00 ET (11:00 PT) — does that work for Michael and your security reviewer?

Regards,
Marissa

marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Acme Health private deployment / VPC options — technical notes

Hi Samantha / Marissa — following up with the technical details we promised. Below is a concise summary. I’m happy to go deeper in the scheduled call.

Key modes we support:
1) VPC-private deployment (no internet egress):
   - Use AWS Gateway/Interface endpoints for S3 and ECR. No NAT required.
   - Model artifacts and benchmarking data accessed via your S3 buckets (we provide IAM role templates and signed URLs for transfer during setup).
   - Metrics/logs: can push to an agent that writes to your S3 or to a metrics collector behind a private endpoint.

2) Fully air-gapped / on-prem bundle:
   - We provide an offline installer (container images + model weights) on encrypted media or transfer over a secure SCP.
   - Requires a short on-site/services engagement (1–2 weeks) to validate environment and baseline health checks.

Minimal networking checklist (examples — to be validated in call):
- Outbound: 0 required if using endpoints. If limited egress enabled for updates/metrics: HTTPS (443) to Redwood update IPs (will provide AAAA/IPv4 ranges).
- Inbound: typically none to the inference cluster; management plane (optional) runs in our control plane or customer-managed VPC depending on deployment.
- Ports between services inside VPC: 443 (TLS) for control/management, 9090 for metrics (optional), ephemeral ports for inter-node gRPC.

KMS/HSM:
- Support for AWS KMS and customer HSMs (PKCS#11). For Luna, we’ve done key wrapping and signing integrations; will need your crypto team to share PKCS#11 endpoints/certs.

Audit/logs / compliance:
- Audit logs can be retained in your S3 with configurable retention.
- SOC2 artifacts: we’ll share a package prior to the deep-dive (see HubSpot link).

Attachment: vpc-networking-notes.txt (short checklist + sample IAM policy).

Happy to adjust the details in the call — looking forward to Tue 14:00 ET.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com
